Latest figures for corn showed a net loss of 2c to 4½c and for oats 1½c to 2½c. In provisions the finish varied from 1½c decline to 1½c advance.

It was shown at the start that Russian and Danubian shipments of wheat had greatly exceeded those of last week and at the corresponding time a year ago. Furthermore, the recent rains in Argentina had continued to weaken Buenos Ayres and European quotations. December wheat here was offered heavily and exerted very bearish influence as it was almost invariably hedged for May delivery by the purchasers. Predictions of rain in the American winter wheat belt, where moisture has been lacking, add to the woes of traders. Exporters declared there was no call by cable for grain from this side of the Atlantic. Cash dealers were almost equally despondent as to domestic demand. Finally, word came that two big mills were to close down at Minneapolis.

Thereafter the market seemed nearly lifeless, though the tone at the finish was steady. During the session May fluctuated from 85½c to 85c, with last sales at 85¼ to 85c, a net loss of 1¼ to 2c.

Foss, newly elected Democratic representative from Massachusetts, a former Republican and a leading manufacturer, today signalized the beginning of his active participation in the house with a radical attack upon the Payne-Aldrich tariff.
